passage: Parul caught Vasudha outside the hostel mess in Pune with a printout of her internship options. "Didi, you know everything. Which one should I take?" Vasudha felt a pleasant flutter at hearing it. She could have simply announced an answer. Instead she read the three offers and said, "I know how the first company runs, because I did it last summer. The other two I've never seen, so don't take my word about them." Then she asked, "What do you want to learn?" Parul chewed her pen. "Maybe design work, not just testing." "Then write to the second one and ask what interns actually do. Tell me what they say." Walking to her room, Vasudha thought that Parul would make her own call, and that felt better than being the expert.

qa.a: She caught Vasudha outside the hostel mess in Pune.

qa.q: What did Vasudha feel when Parul said she knew everything, and how did she handle it?
qa.a: She felt a pleasant flutter but did not use it to announce an answer; she said which offers she knew and asked what Parul wanted to learn.

qa.q: Why was it wise for Vasudha to say she had never seen two of the companies?
qa.a: It kept Parul from trusting guesses as facts and pointed her to ask the company herself. 🙂

qa.q: What is it like for Parul when Vasudha asks what she wants to learn?
qa.a: Parul has to think about her own wishes, and her answer about design work shows she has a view of her own.

grounding: A junior asks for guidance; the senior shares what she knows, admits what she does not and encourages the junior's own view.
